title: Why Don’t Woodpeckers Get Concussions?
description:
Their skulls may not be shock absorbers at all.

Recent research suggests the head acts more like a stiff hammer; small brain size and impact conditions keep pressures below damaging thresholds.

Older shock-absorber explanations are oversimplified, and repeated impacts may still carry biological costs.

A shock-absorbing skull would reduce the efficiency of pecking into wood.
